note.title: Monohybrid crosses, Punnett squares, test crosses and pedigrees
note.subject: science

mustKnow: Genotype: the alleles carried. Phenotype: the characteristic you can see
Homozygous: two alleles the same. Heterozygous: two alleles different
A dominant allele shows whenever it is present; a recessive one only when both alleles are recessive
Four steps: parents' genotypes, gametes, square, count
Two heterozygous parents give 3 : 1 by phenotype and 1 : 2 : 1 by genotype
Higher: a test cross uses a homozygous recessive partner

notOnThisSpec: Crosses that follow two characteristics at once (dihybrid crosses)
The chi-squared test and any statistical test of a ratio

mustBeAbleTo: Define genotype, phenotype, dominant, recessive, homozygous and heterozygous
Say which genotypes give which phenotype, and why two of three look alike
Write the gametes of a genotype as two separate alleles
Fill a Punnett square from the parents' gametes and read the genotype frequencies off it
Give a result as a ratio, a percentage or a probability, in the order the question names
Tell a phenotype ratio from a genotype ratio
Turn a ratio into an expected number of offspring
Higher: describe a test (back) cross and say what each outcome proves
Higher: read genotypes off a pedigree diagram, starting from the recessive individuals
Give the exact relationship between two individuals on a pedigree
sheet.howExamined: B2, 1 hour 15 minutes: 70 marks at Foundation, 80 at Higher, calculator allowed. A late question worth about 7 to 11 marks, opened by a pedigree diagram or by a described cross. Summer 2025 B2 Higher Q8 gave [4] for a two-generation genetic diagram and [3] for describing a test cross; Summer 2025 B2 Foundation Q4 gave the genotype terms and then [4] for a Punnett square with [1] for a percentage; Summer 2024 B2 Higher Q11 ran a pedigree with the relationship, a genotype, a probability and a Punnett square.
traps: Starting a cross from the wrong parental genotype, which costs marks from the first line: Summer 2025 B2 Higher Q8 records it. Read every clue about the parents, such as an offspring showing the recessive phenotype, before you write them down
Not being able to describe a test (back) cross: in Summer 2025 B2 Higher Q8 only the more able candidates could. Name the partner (homozygous recessive), then say what each result would prove
Giving the alleles in the gametes: Summer 2024 B2 Foundation Q5 found fewer candidates could do this than give the parents' genotypes. A sperm or egg cell carries one allele of the pair
Choosing the right Punnett square from several when the format is new: in Summer 2024 B2 Foundation Q5 only the better candidates managed it. Fill the square yourself first, then look for it
Giving 'parent' where the exact relationship, such as father, was wanted (Summer 2024 B2 Higher Q11)
Leaving part of a phenotype out when a word in bold asks for all of it: Summer 2024 B2 Higher Q11 records answers that named the condition but not whether the person was male or female
Not knowing the terms homozygous dominant and homozygous recessive: Summer 2025 B2 Foundation Q4 records that surprisingly few candidates could state them
Using both parental genotypes from an earlier part when the new part names its own (Summer 2023 B2 Foundation Q4)

The Punnett square itself, though it is set most years, still defeated a large number of candidates in Summer 2024 B2 Higher Q11. Write the gametes, then the square: a square drawn correctly from wrong gametes still earns its own marks

steps.working: Parents Bb × Bb. Gametes: B and b from each.
steps.decision: Genotypes first, then gametes. A gamete carries one allele, so each genotype splits into two separate letters.

steps.working: Fill the square: BB, Bb, Bb, bb.
steps.decision: Pair every gamete across the top with every gamete down the side. Work along the top row first so nothing is missed.

options: Because each box is one allele from each parent
Because each box is the genotype of one whole parent
Because each box holds both of a parent's alleles
whyMenu.explain: A box is one offspring, and an offspring gets one allele from each parent. That is why the gametes go round the outside.

steps.decision: Count only what was asked for. chestnut needs bb, so the two Bb boxes do not count.

steps.working: Choose the partner: a chestnut pony, which can only be bb.
steps.decision: The partner has to be an animal whose genotype is certain, and only the recessive phenotype gives that for nothing.

steps.working: If the unknown is Bb: Bb, Bb, bb, bb, so about 50% of the foals are chestnut.
steps.decision: Work out what each possible genotype would produce, before any foals are born. That is what makes the result readable.

steps.working: If the unknown is BB: Bb, Bb, Bb, Bb, so every foal is black.
steps.decision: The two outcomes differ, so one chestnut foal settles it: only the heterozygous parent can produce one.

workedExamples.finalAnswer: Cross it with a chestnut pony: any chestnut foal means heterozygous, all black foals mean homozygous dominant.

items.stem: Before we start, three things from earlier topics. What is an allele?

options.text: a different form of the same gene
options.feedback: A different version of one gene, sitting at the same place on a pair of chromosomes.

options.text: a short length of DNA that controls a characteristic
options.feedback: That is a gene. An allele is one of its versions.

options.text: all of the genetic material of an organism
options.feedback: That is the genome.

options.text: a structure in the nucleus made of DNA
options.feedback: That is a chromosome.

items.stem: How many chromosomes of each pair does a gamete carry?
items.skill: Recall what meiosis does to a pair

options.feedback: One of each pair, which is why a gamete carries one allele of each gene.
Two would be the body cell's number; meiosis halves it.
Four is the number of cells meiosis makes, not the number of chromosomes per pair.
A gamete carries a full single set, one of every pair.

items.stem: 3 of the 4 boxes in a square show one outcome. What percentage is that?
items.skill: Turn a count into a percentage

options.feedback: 3 ÷ 4 × 100 = 75. The same move ends almost every question in this topic.
That is the box left over, not the boxes that show the outcome.
The division is right, but it gives a proportion. Multiply by 100 to turn it into a percentage.
That is the number of boxes, not the percentage.

items.stem: Which word describes a genotype whose two alleles are different?

options.feedback: Hetero means different.
Homo means the same, so that is a genotype whose alleles match.
Dominant describes an allele, not a pair of them.
The phenotype is what you can see.

items.stem: A Shetland pony has the genotype BB, where B is dominant. Which term describes it?

options.feedback: Both alleles the same, and both dominant.
That is bb, where both alleles are the recessive one.
There is no such term: heterozygous already means one of each.
That describes what it looks like, not its pair of alleles.

items.stem: A Bb parent makes gametes. What does each gamete carry?

options.text: one allele, either B or b
options.feedback: One allele each, because meiosis takes one of every pair.
A gamete written as a pair is the commonest slip in this topic.

options.text: two alleles the same, BB or bb
options.feedback: That is a genotype, not a gamete.
A gamete carries a full single set of alleles, one per gene.

items.stem: Two Bb parents are crossed. Which set of genotypes fills the four boxes of the Punnett square?

options.text: one BB, two Bb and one bb
options.feedback: B with B gives BB, B with b gives Bb, and b with b gives bb.
That would need every pairing to be one of each, which the gametes make impossible.

options.text: two BB and two bb, with no heterozygous box
options.feedback: That pairs each parent with itself instead of across the square.

options.text: B, b, B, b, the gametes copied into the boxes
options.feedback: Those are the gametes copied into the boxes.

items.stem: A Bb × Bb cross gives what phenotype ratio, black to chestnut?
items.skill: Give a phenotype ratio the right way round

options.feedback: 3 boxes show the dominant coat and 1 shows the recessive one.
That is the same ratio written backwards, and the order follows the question.
That is the genotype ratio, which counts BB and Bb apart.
An even split is what a cross with a homozygous recessive parent gives, not this one.

items.stem: In the same cross, what percentage of the offspring are expected to be chestnut?
items.skill: Turn a ratio into a percentage

options.feedback: One box in four, so 25%.
That is the percentage with the dominant phenotype.
That counts the two heterozygous boxes, which show the dominant coat.
That reads 3 : 1 as one in three; the two numbers add to four.

items.stem: In a test cross, what genotype must the partner have?

options.feedback: Only then is the partner's contribution certain, so the offspring reveal the unknown parent.
Its dominant allele would hide whatever the unknown parent gave.
That leaves two unknowns instead of one.

options.text: the same as the unknown parent
options.feedback: The whole point is that the unknown parent's genotype is not known.

The first is a gamete written as a pair of letters: a gamete carries one allele, and an answer that gives both loses the point about gametes and usually the one after it. parts.workedSolution: A dominant allele shows in the phenotype whenever it is present, so a black pony can be either BB or Bb. Since one of the foals is chestnut, and the chestnut coat only appears when both alleles are recessive, that foal must be bb. It received one recessive allele from each parent, so both parents must be heterozygous, carrying one dominant and one recessive allele. Each parent's gametes carry one allele, so each parent can pass on either the dominant or the recessive one. A foal that receives the recessive allele from both parents is homozygous recessive and shows the chestnut coat, and about 25% of the foals of such a cross are expected to be chestnut, a ratio of 3 : 1. To find the genotype of a black pony, a breeder carries out a test cross: the unknown animal is crossed with a chestnut one, which must be homozygous recessive. Any offspring showing the recessive phenotype proves the unknown parent is heterozygous, while all the offspring showing the dominant phenotype points to homozygous dominant.

Méabh is asked: 'Describe how a breeder could carry out a test cross on a black Shetland pony. [3]'

prompts.answer: The genotype is the alleles an organism carries for a characteristic. The phenotype is the characteristic you can see.

prompts.prompt: Give the three terms for the genotypes BB, bb and Bb, where B is dominant.
prompts.answer: BB is homozygous dominant, bb is homozygous recessive and Bb is heterozygous.

prompts.prompt: Give the four steps of working out a cross, in order.
prompts.answer: Parents' genotypes, then gametes, then the offspring in the square, then count what the question asks for.

prompts.prompt: How many alleles does a gamete carry for one characteristic, and why?
prompts.answer: One, because meiosis puts one chromosome of each pair into each gamete.

prompts.prompt: What phenotype ratio does a cross between two heterozygous parents give, and what percentage shows the recessive phenotype?
What is the difference between a phenotype ratio and a genotype ratio for one gene with two alleles?
prompts.answer: The phenotype ratio has two numbers, 3 : 1, because the two dominant genotypes look alike. The genotype ratio has three, 1 : 2 : 1, because it counts them apart.

prompts.prompt: Describe a test cross in one sentence, and say what each result proves.
prompts.answer: Cross the unknown with a homozygous recessive animal: any recessive offspring proves it is heterozygous, and all-dominant offspring point to homozygous dominant.

prompts.prompt: On a pedigree diagram, which individuals give you a certain genotype straight away?
prompts.answer: The ones showing the recessive phenotype: they must be homozygous recessive.

prompts.prompt: In tomato plants, tall (T) is dominant to short (t). Two Tt plants are crossed. What fraction of the offspring is expected to be short?
prompts.answer: One quarter, because only tt gives a short plant and one box in four is tt.

prompts.prompt: A question's part (b) names its own two parents. What must you do with the genotypes from part (a)?
prompts.answer: Leave them behind. Each part names the animals it is about, and carrying the earlier pair over loses the mark.

findings.asked: A pedigree and a cross: name the relationship, give genotypes, then cross a specified (bold) individual.
findings.wentWrong: The relationship had to be exact ('father', not 'parent'); many read past the bold word 'complete' and named the condition without the sex; and the Punnett square - examined many times - was still often wrong, though a correct cross from wrong gametes earned error-carried-forward marks.
findings.fullMarkAnswersDid: Read the bold words twice, wrote the parental genotypes, then the gametes, then the square.
findings.rule: Bold words in a genetics stem are the whole question; genotypes before gametes before square.

findings.asked: A cross over two generations from a described situation, then a description of a test (back) cross.
findings.wentWrong: Some started from the wrong parental genotype so everything after it was wrong; only the more able could describe a test cross.
findings.rule: A test cross uses a homozygous recessive partner: any recessive offspring proves the unknown parent is heterozygous.

findings.asked: State the genotype terms for given allele pairs, draw a Punnett square and give a percentage.
findings.wentWrong: Surprisingly few could write 'homozygous dominant' and 'homozygous recessive'; the square itself was mostly right (three of four marks common) and 50% was often found.
findings.rule: Homozygous = two identical alleles (dominant or recessive); heterozygous = one of each.

findings.asked: Parental genotypes and alleles, then choose the correct Punnett squares from options.
findings.wentWrong: Genotypes were given by quite a few but the alleles by fewer; the unfamiliar 'choose the square' format was managed only by the better candidates.
findings.rule: An allele is one letter; a genotype is the pair.

insight.ruleToRemember: Write the parents' genotypes first (obey the bold words), then their gametes, then the square, then count the ratio or percentage the question asks for. Homozygous = two identical alleles, heterozygous = different; a test cross uses a homozygous recessive partner.
insight.aStarSignal: Correct genotypes from a pedigree with the reasoning stated, then a test cross explained in terms of what the offspring would reveal.
